title.zh: 卷48 列傳第13 楊素
title.raw: 卷48 列傳第13 楊素 Volume 48 Biographies 13: Yang Su

sentences.zh: 楊素，字處道，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Su, styled Chudao, was a native of Huayin in Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, whose courtesy name was Chudao, came from Huayin in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 祖暄，魏輔國將軍、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan was General Who Assists the State of Wei and Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan had been General Who Assists the State and grand master of remonstrance under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父敷，周汾州刺史，沒于齊。

translations.literal: His father Fu was Governor of Fen Province under Zhou and died in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu served as governor of Fen Province under the Zhou and perished in Qi captivity.

sentences.zh: 素少落拓，有大志，不拘小節，世人多未之知，唯從叔祖魏尚書僕射寬深異之，每謂子孫曰：「處道當逸群絕倫，非常之器，非汝曹所逮也。」

translations.literal: Su in youth was unrestrained and had great ambition, not bound by petty propriety; most of the world did not yet know him. Only his father's younger cousin, Wei Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Kuan, regarded him as deeply extraordinary and often told his descendants: "Chudao will surpass the crowd and stand alone—an instrument of no ordinary kind, not something you can reach."
translations.idiomatic: In youth Su was free-spirited and ambitious, careless of small conventions; few knew him yet. Only his father's younger cousin, Wei Vice Director Kuan, saw something remarkable in him and often told his descendants, "Chudao will outstrip all others—no ordinary talent, and not one you can match.

sentences.zh: 後與安定牛弘同志好學，研精不倦，多所通涉。

translations.literal: Later he shared the same ideals with Niu Hong of Anding, loved learning together, studied with tireless depth, and mastered many fields.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied alongside Niu Hong of Anding, reading deeply without tiring and gaining wide mastery.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，工草隸，頗留意於風角。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composition, adept at cursive and clerical script, and paid considerable attention to wind-and-angle divination.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well, excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy, and took a keen interest in wind-and-angle divination.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，有英傑之表。

translations.literal: His beard and whiskers were handsome, and he had the bearing of a hero.
translations.idiomatic: With a fine beard and commanding looks, he had the air of a hero.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外記室，後轉禮曹，加大都督。

translations.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of Zhou, brought him in as recorder of the central and exterior headquarters staff; later he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites and promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, Zhou's grand minister, appointed him recorder in the central and exterior staff; later he moved to the Ministry of Rites and was made grand commander.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，素以其父守節陷齊，未蒙朝命，上表申理，帝不許。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally handled all affairs of state, Su, because his father had kept faith and fallen into Qi, had not received court honors, submitted a memorial to plead his case, and the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took direct control of government, Su—whose father had held firm and died in Qi—had received no posthumous honors from court. He memorialized to plead the case, and the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 至於再三，帝大怒，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: When he did so again and again, the emperor grew furious and ordered his attendants to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: After he persisted, the emperor flew into a rage and ordered his attendants to behead him.

sentences.zh: 素乃大言曰：「臣事無道天子，死其分也。」

translations.literal: Su then spoke boldly: "Your servant serves a wayless Son of Heaven; death is my portion."
translations.idiomatic: Su cried out boldly, "I serve a lawless emperor—death is only what I deserve.

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，由是贈敷為大將軍，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his words; thereupon Fu was posthumously made Grand General with the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed by his courage and posthumously made Fu grand general with the title Loyal and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 拜素為車騎大將軍、儀同三司，漸見禮遇。

translations.literal: Su was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Threefold Peerage; he gradually came to receive courteous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Su was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry with threefold peerage rank and gradually won favor at court.

sentences.zh: 帝命素為詔書，下筆立成，詞義兼美。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Su to draft an edict; he wrote at once, and the wording and meaning were both fine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Su draft an edict; he finished at a stroke, with wording and sense alike polished.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，顧謂素曰：「善自勉之，勿憂不富貴。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and, turning to Su, said: "Strive hard yourself; do not worry that you will lack wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and said, "Apply yourself—you need not fear missing out on wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 素應聲答曰：「臣但恐富貴來逼臣，臣無心圖富貴。」

translations.literal: Su answered at once: "Your servant only fears that wealth and rank will press upon me; I have no mind to seek them."
translations.idiomatic: Su answered at once, "I only fear wealth and rank closing in on me—I have no wish to pursue them."

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，素深自結納。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Su attached himself to him with deep devotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor, Su bound himself closely to him.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚器之，以素為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: Gaozu greatly valued him and made Su Governor of Bian Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thought highly of him and appointed him governor of Bian Province.

sentences.zh: 行至洛陽，會尉迥作亂，滎州刺史宇文胄據武牢以應迥，素不得進。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, Wei Chiyuan rebelled; Yuwen Zhou, Governor of Xing Province, held Wulao in response to Chiyuan, and Su could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Luoyang he found Wei Chiyuan in revolt; Xing governor Yuwen Zhou held Wulao in support, blocking Su's advance.

sentences.zh: 高祖拜素大將軍，發河內兵擊胄，破之。

translations.literal: Gaozu appointed Su Grand General, raised troops from Henei, attacked Zhou, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made Su grand general, raised Henei troops, attacked Zhou, and broke him.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州總管，進位柱國，封清河郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou, advanced to Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Xuzhou, promoted to pillar of the state, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 以弟岳為臨貞公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yue was made Duke of Linzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yue was made Duke of Linzhen.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加上柱國。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Su was further made Supreme Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Su was further made supreme pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 4 he was appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其妻鄭氏性悍，素忿之曰：「我若作天子，卿定不堪為皇后。」

translations.literal: His wife Lady Zheng was fierce by nature; Su said in anger: "If I were to become Son of Heaven, you surely could not bear to be empress."
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Zheng was sharp-tempered; Su snapped, "If I were emperor, you could never be empress.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏奏之，由是坐免。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng reported it, and for this he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng reported him, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 上方圖江表，先是，素數進取陳之計，未幾，拜信州總管，賜錢百萬、錦千段、馬二百匹而遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor was then planning for the lands south of the Yangzi; earlier Su had repeatedly urged plans to take Chen. Before long he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Xin Province, given a million coins, a thousand bolts of brocade, and two hundred horses, and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was planning the conquest of the south; Su had long urged schemes against Chen. Soon he was made commander of Xin Province, given a million coins, a thousand bolts of brocade, and two hundred horses, and dispatched.

sentences.zh: 素居永安，造大艦，名曰五牙，上起樓五層，高百餘尺，左右前後置六拍竿，並高五十尺，容戰士八百人，旗幟加於上。

translations.literal: Su stayed at Yong'an and built great ships called Five-Tooth, with five-story towers more than a hundred feet high; on front, rear, left, and right he placed six battering poles, each fifty feet high, holding eight hundred warriors, with banners and flags set above.
translations.idiomatic: At Yong'an Su built great warships called Five-Tooth: five-story towers over a hundred feet high, six battering poles fifty feet tall on every side, each holding eight hundred fighters under banners and flags.

sentences.zh: 次曰黃龍，置兵百人。

translations.literal: Next came the Yellow Dragon, each holding a hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Yellow Dragon class, each carrying a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 自餘平乘、舴艋等各有差。

translations.literal: The rest—flat boats, skiffs, and the like—varied in size.
translations.idiomatic: Other flat boats and skiffs followed in graded sizes.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以素為行軍元帥，引舟師趣三硤。

translations.literal: When a great campaign was launched against Chen, Su was made campaign commander-in-chief and led the fleet toward the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: When the great assault on Chen began, Su was made campaign commander and led the fleet toward the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 軍至流頭灘，陳將戚欣以青龍百餘艘、屯兵數千人守狼尾灘，以遏軍路。

translations.literal: When the army reached Liutou Shoals, Chen general Qi Xin, with more than a hundred Green Dragon ships and several thousand troops, held Langwei Shoals to block the army's route.
translations.idiomatic: At Liutou Shoals Chen general Qi Xin held Langwei with over a hundred Green Dragon ships and several thousand men, blocking the route.

sentences.zh: 其地險峭，諸將患之。

translations.literal: The ground was steep and perilous, and the generals were troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain was steep and dangerous, and the generals were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「勝負大計，在此一舉。

translations.literal: Su said: "Victory or defeat hangs on this one move.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Victory or defeat turns on this one stroke.

sentences.zh: 若晝日下船，彼則見我，灘流迅激，制不由人，則吾失其便。」

translations.literal: If we land by day, they will see us; the shoal currents are swift and violent, and control is not in men's hands—we would lose our advantage."
translations.idiomatic: If we land by day they will see us; the shoal runs fast and cannot be controlled—we would lose our chance.

sentences.zh: 乃以夜掩之。

translations.literal: So he struck by night.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked by night.

sentences.zh: 素親率黃龍數千艘，銜枚而下，遣開府王長襲引步卒從南岸擊欣別柵，令大將軍劉仁恩率甲騎趣白沙北岸，遲明而至，擊之，欣敗走。

translations.literal: Su personally led several thousand Yellow Dragon ships down with gags in the men's mouths, sent Colonel Wang Changxi to lead foot soldiers from the south bank against Xin's outpost palisade, and ordered Grand General Liu Ren'en to lead armored cavalry toward the north bank of Baisha; at daybreak they arrived, attacked, and Xin was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Su himself led thousands of Yellow Dragon ships down with men gagged for silence, sent Colonel Wang Changxi against Xin's outpost from the south bank, and Grand General Liu Ren'en with armored cavalry to Baisha's north bank; at dawn they struck and Xin fled.

sentences.zh: 悉虜其眾，勞而遣之，秋毫不犯，陳人大悅。

translations.literal: He captured the whole force, treated them kindly and sent them off, and did not violate so much as a hair; the people of Chen were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He took all their men, treated them kindly, and sent them off without the least harm; the Chen people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 素率水軍東下，舟艫被江，旌甲曜日。

translations.literal: Su led the fleet eastward; ships covered the river, banners and armor gleaming in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Su's fleet moved east; the river was covered with ships, banners and armor blazing in sunlight.

sentences.zh: 素坐平乘大船，容貌雄偉，陳人望之懼曰：「清河公即江神也。」

translations.literal: Su sat in a flat boat, his appearance imposing; the people of Chen looked on in fear and said: "The Duke of Qinghe is the river god himself."
translations.idiomatic: Su sat in an open boat, imposing in bearing; Chen people looked on in dread and said, "The Duke of Qinghe is the river god incarnate.

sentences.zh: 陳南康內史呂仲肅屯岐亭，正據江峽，於北岸鑿岩，綴鐵鎖三條，橫截上流，以遏戰船。

translations.literal: Chen Interior Minister of Nankang Lü Zhongsu held at Qiting, directly commanding the river gorge; on the north bank he cut into the cliff, joined three iron chains, and stretched them across the upper stream to block the warships.
translations.idiomatic: Chen interior minister Lü Zhongsu held Qiting at the gorge, cut the north-bank cliff, and stretched three iron chains across the upper stream to block the fleet.

sentences.zh: 素與仁恩登陸俱發，先攻其柵。

translations.literal: Su and Ren'en landed together and attacked, first striking the palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Ren'en landed together and first stormed the palisade.

sentences.zh: 仲肅軍夜潰，素徐去其鎖。

translations.literal: Zhongsu's army collapsed by night; Su slowly removed the chains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu's army broke by night; Su removed the chains at leisure.

sentences.zh: 仲肅複據荊門之延洲。

translations.literal: Zhongsu again held Yanzhou at Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu rallied at Yanzhou in Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 素遣巴蜒卒千人，乘五牙四艘，以柏檣碎賊十餘艦，遂大破之，俘甲士二千余人，仲肅僅以身免。

translations.literal: Su sent a thousand Bayan soldiers in four Five-Tooth ships; with cypress rams they smashed more than ten enemy vessels, routed them completely, captured more than two thousand armored men, and Zhongsu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent a thousand Bayan troops in four Five-Tooth ships; with cypress rams they shattered a dozen enemy ships, took two thousand armored men, and Zhongsu barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 陳主遣其信州刺史顧覺鎮安蜀城，荊州刺史陳紀鎮公安，皆懾而退走。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler sent his Governor of Xin Province Gu Jue to hold Anshu and Governor Chen Ji to hold Gong'an; both were afraid and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler posted Xin governor Gu Jue at Anshu and Jing governor Chen Ji at Gong'an; both fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 巴陵以東，無敢守者。

translations.literal: East of Baling, none dared hold out.
translations.idiomatic: East of Baling none dared stand guard.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史、岳陽王陳叔慎遣使請降。

translations.literal: Xiang Governor and Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushen sent envoys to offer surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang governor and Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushen sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 素下至漢口，與秦孝王會。

translations.literal: Su went down to Hankou and joined Prince Xiao of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Su descended to Hankou and joined Prince Xiao of Qin.

sentences.zh: 及還，拜荊州總管，進爵郢國公，邑三千戶，真食長壽縣千戶。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Jing Province, advanced to Duke of Ying, with a fief of three thousand households and direct sustenance from a thousand households of Changshou county.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made commander of Jing Province, promoted to Duke of Ying with three thousand households and direct income from a thousand in Changshou.

sentences.zh: 以其子玄感為儀同，玄獎為清河郡公。

translations.literal: His son Xuangan was made Threefold Peerage, and Xuanjiang Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuangan was made threefold peerage, and Xuanjiang duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 賜物萬段，粟萬石，加以金寶，又賜陳主妹及女妓十四人。

translations.literal: He was given ten thousand bolts of goods and ten thousand shi of grain, with gold and jewels added, and also the Chen ruler's younger sister and fourteen female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: He received ten thousand bolts of goods, ten thousand shi of grain, gold and jewels, the Chen ruler's younger sister, and fourteen female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 素言於上曰：「裡名勝母，曾子不入。

translations.literal: Su said to the emperor: "A lane named Shengmu—Zengzi would not enter it.
translations.idiomatic: Su told the emperor, "There is a lane called Shengmu; even Zengzi would not enter it.

sentences.zh: 逆人王誼，前封於郢，臣不願與之同。」

translations.literal: The rebel Wang Yi was formerly enfeoffed at Ying; your servant does not wish to share that place."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Wang Yi had been enfeoffed at Ying; I do not wish to share that title.

sentences.zh: 於是改封越國公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yue.

sentences.zh: 尋拜納言。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉內史令。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he became director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄而江南人李稜等聚眾為亂，大者數萬，小者數千，共相影響，殺害長吏。

translations.literal: Before long Li Ling and others of the Jiangnan region gathered crowds in rebellion; the large bands numbered tens of thousands, the small several thousand; they echoed one another and killed local officials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Ling and other Jiangnan men raised bands—some tens of thousands strong, some only thousands—echoing one another and killing local officials.

sentences.zh: 以素為行軍總管，帥眾討之。

translations.literal: Su was made campaign commander-in-chief and led troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Su was made campaign commander and marched to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 賊硃莫問自稱南徐州刺史，以盛兵據京口。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhu Mowen styled himself Governor of South Xuzhou and with a strong force held Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhu Mowen styled himself governor of South Xuzhou and held Jingkou with a large force.

sentences.zh: 素率舟師入自楊子津，進擊破之。

translations.literal: Su led the fleet in from Yangzi Ford and advanced to attack and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Su led the fleet in through Yangzi Ford and routed him.

sentences.zh: 晉陵顧世興自稱太守，與其都督鮑遷等複來拒戰。

translations.literal: Gu Shixing of Jinling styled himself governor and, with his commander Bao Qian and others, again came to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shixing of Jinling styled himself governor and, with commander Bao Qian and others, resisted again.

sentences.zh: 素逆擊破之，執遷，虜三千餘人。

translations.literal: Su met and defeated them, captured Qian, and took more than three thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Su met and broke them, captured Qian, and took more than three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 進擊無錫賊帥葉略，又平之。

translations.literal: Advancing he attacked the Wuxi bandit chief Ye Lüe and pacified him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing he attacked Wuxi bandit chief Ye Lüe and pacified him too.

sentences.zh: 吳郡沈玄懀、沈傑等以兵圍蘇州，刺史皇甫績頻戰不利。

translations.literal: Shen Xuanyi and Shen Jie of Wu commandery and others besieged Suzhou with troops; Governor Huangfu Ji fought repeatedly without success.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xuanyi and Shen Jie of Wu besieged Suzhou; governor Huangfu Ji fought repeatedly and fared badly.

sentences.zh: 素率眾援之，玄懀勢迫，走投南沙賊帥陸孟孫。

translations.literal: Su led troops to rescue him; Xuanyi was hard pressed, fled, and threw himself on Nansha bandit chief Lu Mengsun.
translations.idiomatic: Su marched to relieve the city; Xuanyi, pressed hard, fled to Nansha bandit chief Lu Mengsun.

sentences.zh: 素擊孟孫于松江，大破之，生擒孟孫、玄懀。

translations.literal: Su attacked Mengsun on Song River, routed him completely, and captured Mengsun and Xuanyi alive.
translations.idiomatic: Su struck Mengsun on the Song River, broke him completely, and took Mengsun and Xuanyi alive.

sentences.zh: 黟、歙賊帥沈雪、沈能據柵自固，又攻拔之。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Shen Xue and Shen Neng of Yi and She held palisades in strength; he attacked and took them too.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chiefs Shen Xue and Shen Neng of Yi and She held fortified palisades; he stormed and took them as well.

sentences.zh: 浙江賊帥高智慧自號東揚州刺史，船艦千艘，屯據要害，兵甚勁。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang bandit chief Gao Zhihui styled himself Governor of East Yangzhou; he had a thousand ships and held key points with very strong troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang bandit chief Gao Zhihui styled himself governor of East Yangzhou; with a thousand ships he held key points and fielded fierce troops.

sentences.zh: 素擊之，自旦至申，苦戰而破。

translations.literal: Su attacked him; from dawn to the shen hour he fought bitterly and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Su attacked from dawn to mid-afternoon in bitter fighting and broke him.

sentences.zh: 智慧逃入海，素躡之，從餘姚泛海趣永嘉。

translations.literal: Zhihui fled to sea; Su pursued him, going from Yuyao by sea toward Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui fled to sea; Su pursued from Yuyao by sea toward Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 智慧來拒戰，素擊走之，擒獲數千人。

translations.literal: Zhihui came to resist; Su attacked and drove him off and captured several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui resisted; Su drove him off and captured several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 賊帥汪文進自稱天子，據東陽，署其徒蔡道人為司空，守樂安。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Wang Wenjin styled himself Son of Heaven, held Dongyang, appointed his follower Cai Daoren Minister of Works, and garrisoned Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chief Wang Wenjin styled himself Son of Heaven, held Dongyang, made follower Cai Daoren minister of works, and garrisoned Le'an.

sentences.zh: 進討，悉平之。

translations.literal: Su advanced to attack and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Su advanced and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 又破永嘉賊帥沈孝徹。

translations.literal: He also defeated the Yongjia bandit chief Shen Xiaoche.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Yongjia bandit chief Shen Xiaoche.

sentences.zh: 於是步道向天臺，指臨海郡，逐捕遺逸寇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he marched overland toward Tiantai, aiming at Linhai commandery, hunting down scattered bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched overland toward Tiantai and Linhai, hunting down scattered rebels.

sentences.zh: 前後百餘戰，智慧遁守閩越。

translations.literal: In more than a hundred battles before and after, Zhihui fled to hold Min and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a hundred battles Zhihui fled to hold out in Min and Yue.

sentences.zh: 上以素久勞於外，詔令馳傳入朝。

translations.literal: Because Su had long toiled outside, the emperor ordered him to enter court by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing Su's long service in the field, ordered him to court by post relay.

sentences.zh: 加子玄感官為上開府，賜彩物三千段。

translations.literal: Su's son Xuangan was further made Upper Threefold Peerage, and three thousand bolts of colored goods were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son Xuangan was further made upper threefold peerage, and he received three thousand bolts of colored goods.

sentences.zh: 素以餘賊未殄，恐為後患，又自請行。

translations.literal: Su, because remaining bandits were not yet destroyed and he feared they would become a later trouble, again asked to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing surviving rebels would become a later threat, Su asked to go again himself.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「朕憂勞百姓，日旰忘食，一物失所，情深納隍。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "We worry and toil for the people, forgetting to eat until the sun sets; if one thing is lost from its place, our feeling is as deep as falling into a moat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "We toil for the people, forgetting meals until sunset; if one thing is out of place, our grief is bottomless.

sentences.zh: 江外狂狡，妄構妖逆，雖經殄除，民未安堵。

translations.literal: Outside the river, wild and cunning men falsely raised demonic rebellion; though they have been destroyed, the people are not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi, wild rebels raised false rebellion; though crushed, the people are not yet at peace.

sentences.zh: 猶有賊首凶魁，逃亡山洞，恐其聚結，重擾蒼生。

translations.literal: There are still bandit chiefs and evil ringleaders hiding in mountain caves; fearing they may gather and again trouble the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit chiefs still hide in mountain caves, and we fear they may gather and trouble the people again.

sentences.zh: 內史令、上柱國、越國公素，識達古今，經謀長遠，比曾推轂，舊著威名，宜任以大兵，總為元帥，宣佈朝風，振揚威武，擒剪叛亡，慰勞黎庶。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Duke of Yue Su understands past and present, plans far ahead, and in former campaigns has shown his old renown; he should be entrusted with great forces as overall commander, proclaim the court's ways, display martial might, capture and cut down rebels, and comfort the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Director Su, supreme pillar and Duke of Yue, knows past and present and plans far ahead; in earlier campaigns he proved his name—let him command great forces, proclaim court policy, show martial might, cut down rebels, and comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 軍民事務，一以委之。」

translations.literal: Military and civil affairs—all are entrusted to him."
translations.idiomatic: Military and civil affairs are wholly entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 素複乘傳至會稽。

translations.literal: Su again went by post relay to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Su again went by post relay to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 先是，泉州人王國慶，南安豪族也，殺刺史劉弘，據州為亂，諸亡賊皆歸之。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Guoqing of Quanzhou, a great clan of Nan'an, had killed Governor Liu Hong, seized the province in rebellion, and all fugitive bandits joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Guoqing of Quanzhou, a Nan'an magnate, had killed governor Liu Hong, seized the province, and drawn every fugitive rebel to him.

sentences.zh: 自以海路艱阻，非北人所習，不設備伍。

translations.literal: He thought the sea route hard and perilous and unfamiliar to northerners, and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking the sea route hard and unknown to northerners, he made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 素泛海掩至，國慶遑遽，棄州而走，餘黨散入海島，或守溪洞。

translations.literal: Su crossed the sea and struck suddenly; Guoqing was alarmed, abandoned the province and fled, and the remnant bands scattered to sea islands or held stream caves.
translations.idiomatic: Su crossed the sea and struck by surprise; Guoqing fled in alarm, and remnants scattered to islands and stream caves.

sentences.zh: 素分遣諸將，水陸追捕。

translations.literal: Su sent out his generals to pursue by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent generals to pursue by land and water.

sentences.zh: 乃密令人謂國慶曰：「爾之罪狀，計不容誅。

translations.literal: He then secretly sent someone to tell Guoqing: "Your crimes, by reckoning, cannot escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly sent word to Guoqing: "Your crimes merit death beyond question.

sentences.zh: 唯有斬送智慧，可以塞責。」

translations.literal: Only by beheading and sending Zhihui can you answer for them."
translations.idiomatic: Only by sending Zhihui's head can you atone.

sentences.zh: 國慶於是執送智慧，斬於泉州。

translations.literal: Guoqing thereupon seized and sent Zhihui, who was executed at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqing seized Zhihui and sent him; he was executed at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 自餘支黨，悉來降附，江南大定。

translations.literal: The remaining factions all came to surrender; the Jiangnan region was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining factions surrendered; Jiangnan was largely pacified.

sentences.zh: 上遣左領軍將軍獨孤陀至浚儀迎勞。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Left Palace Guard General Dugu Tuo to Junyi to welcome and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Left Palace Guard General Dugu Tuo to Junyi to welcome and reward him.

sentences.zh: 比到京師，問者日至。

translations.literal: By the time he reached the capital, visitors came daily.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the capital, callers came every day.

sentences.zh: 拜素子玄獎為儀同，賜黃金四十斤，加銀瓶，實以金錢，縑三千段，馬二百匹，羊二千口，公田百頃，宅一區。

translations.literal: Su's son Xuanjiang was made Threefold Peerage; he was given forty jin of gold, a silver bottle filled with gold coins, three thousand bolts of silk, two hundred horses, two thousand sheep, a hundred qing of public fields, and one residence.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son Xuanjiang was made threefold peerage; he received forty jin of gold, a silver bottle of gold coins, three thousand bolts of silk, two hundred horses, two thousand sheep, a hundred qing of public land, and a mansion.

sentences.zh: 代蘇威為尚書右僕射，與高熲專掌朝政。

translations.literal: He replaced Su Wei as Vice Director of the Right in the Masters of Writing and, with Gao Jiong, jointly managed court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Su Wei as right vice director of the Masters of Writing and, with Gao Jiong, jointly ran court governance.

sentences.zh: 素性疏而辯，高下在心，朝臣之內，頗推高熲，敬牛弘，厚接薛道衡，視蘇威蔑如也。

translations.literal: Su by nature was blunt yet eloquent; high and low were in his heart; among court ministers he fairly esteemed Gao Jiong, respected Niu Hong, treated Xue Daoheng warmly, and looked on Su Wei with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Su was blunt yet eloquent, with everyone's rank fixed in his mind; among ministers he fairly esteemed Gao Jiong, respected Niu Hong, favored Xue Daoheng, and despised Su Wei.

sentences.zh: 自餘朝貴，多被陵轢。

translations.literal: The rest of the court nobles were mostly bullied by him.
translations.idiomatic: Most other court grandees he bullied.

sentences.zh: 其才藝風調，優於高熲，至於推誠體國，處物平當，有宰相識度，不如熲遠矣。

translations.literal: In talent, style, and bearing he surpassed Gao Jiong; yet in sincere devotion to the state and fair handling of affairs, and in the discernment of a chief minister, he fell far short of Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: In talent and bearing he outshone Gao Jiong; in sincere service to the state, fair dealing, and ministerial judgment he fell far short.

sentences.zh: 尋令素監營仁壽宮，素遂夷山堙穀，督役嚴急，作者多死，宮側時聞鬼哭之聲。

translations.literal: Soon Su was ordered to supervise construction of Renshou Palace; he leveled mountains and filled valleys, pressing the labor with harsh urgency; many workers died, and by the palace one sometimes heard the sound of ghosts weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Su was ordered to oversee Renshou Palace; he leveled mountains and filled valleys with brutal urgency. Many laborers died, and ghostly weeping was heard beside the palace.

sentences.zh: 及宮成，上令高熲前視，奏稱頗傷綺麗，大損人丁，高祖不悅。

translations.literal: When the palace was finished, the emperor ordered Gao Jiong to inspect it first; he reported that it was overly lavish and had wasted many lives, and Gaozu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace was done, the emperor sent Gao Jiong to inspect it; he reported excessive splendor and great loss of life, and Gaozu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 素尤懼，計無所出，即於北門啟獨孤皇后曰：「帝王法有離宮別館，今天下太平，造此一宮，何足損費！」

translations.literal: Su was especially afraid and knew no way out; he then opened the north gate and told Empress Dugu alone: "The law of emperors and kings provides detached palaces; now the realm is at peace—what harm is one palace?"
translations.idiomatic: Su was terrified and at a loss; he went to Empress Dugu at the north gate and said, "Emperors keep detached palaces by law; with peace under heaven, what harm is one palace?

sentences.zh: 後以此理諭上，上意乃解。

translations.literal: The empress used this reasoning to persuade the emperor, and the emperor's mind was eased.
translations.idiomatic: The empress used this to persuade the emperor, and his anger lifted.

sentences.zh: 於是賜錢百萬，錦絹三千段。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given a million coins and three thousand bolts of brocade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a million coins and three thousand bolts of brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 十八年，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，以素為靈州道行軍總管，出塞討之，賜物二千段，黃金百斤。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when Tardu Khan of the Turks invaded the frontier, Su was made campaign commander-in-chief of the Lingzhou route, went beyond the passes to attack him, and was given two thousand bolts of goods and a hundred jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, when Tardu Khan of the Turks raided the frontier, Su was made Lingzhou-route campaign commander, marched beyond the passes, and received two thousand bolts of goods and a hundred jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸將與虜戰，每慮胡騎奔突，皆以戎車步騎相參，輿鹿角為方陣，騎在其內。

translations.literal: Earlier, when generals fought the barbarians they always feared Turk cavalry charges and therefore mixed war chariots with infantry and cavalry, using carts and antlers to form square formations with cavalry inside.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier generals fighting the Turks, fearing cavalry charges, mixed chariots with infantry and cavalry in cart-and-antler squares with horsemen inside.

sentences.zh: 素謂人曰：「此乃自固之道，非取勝之方也。」

translations.literal: Su told others: "This is a way to protect oneself, not a method for victory.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "That is self-defense, not a way to win.

sentences.zh: 於是悉除舊法，令諸軍為騎陣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he completely abolished the old method and ordered all armies into cavalry formations.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the old method and ordered pure cavalry formations.

sentences.zh: 達頭聞之大喜，曰：「此天賜我也。」

translations.literal: When Tardu heard this he was greatly pleased and said: "Heaven has given this to me.
translations.idiomatic: Tardu was delighted and said, "Heaven has handed this to me.

sentences.zh: 因下馬仰天而拜，率精騎十余萬而至。

translations.literal: He then dismounted, bowed to heaven, and led more than a hundred thousand picked horsemen to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, bowed to heaven, and led more than a hundred thousand picked horsemen forward.

sentences.zh: 素奮擊，大破之，達頭被重創而遁，殺傷不可勝計，群虜號哭而去。

translations.literal: Su struck hard and routed them completely; Tardu was gravely wounded and fled; the dead and wounded were beyond counting, and the barbarian hosts wailed as they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Su struck hard and routed them; Tardu was gravely wounded and fled; casualties were beyond count, and the tribes wailed as they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒揚，賜縑二萬匹，及萬釘寶帶。

translations.literal: A gracious edict praised him; he was given twenty thousand bolts of silk and a treasure belt studded with ten thousand nails.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him; he received twenty thousand bolts of silk and a ten-thousand-nail treasure belt.

sentences.zh: 加子玄感位大將軍，玄獎、玄縱、積善並上儀同。

translations.literal: Su's son Xuangan was further made Grand General; Xuanjiang, Xuanzong, and Jishan were all made Upper Threefold Peerage.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son Xuangan was further made grand general; Xuanjiang, Xuanzong, and Jishan all became upper threefold peerage.

sentences.zh: 素多權略，乘機赴敵，應變無方，然大抵馭戎嚴整，有犯軍令者立斬之，無所寬貸。

translations.literal: Su had many stratagems; seizing the moment to meet the enemy and adapting without fixed method—yet in general he governed troops with strict order; whoever violated military law was beheaded at once, with no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Su was full of stratagems, seizing moments and adapting without fixed method; yet he ruled troops with iron discipline—any breach of military law meant instant execution.

sentences.zh: 每將臨寇，輒求人過失而斬之，多者百餘人，少不下十數。

translations.literal: Each time he was about to face the enemy he would seek men's faults and behead them—sometimes more than a hundred, never fewer than a dozen.
translations.idiomatic: Before each battle he would find men's faults and behead them—sometimes more than a hundred, never fewer than ten.

sentences.zh: 流血盈前，言笑自若。

translations.literal: Blood filled the ground before him, yet he spoke and laughed as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Blood pooled before him while he spoke and laughed as if at ease.

sentences.zh: 及其對陣，先令一二百人赴敵，陷陣則已，如不能陷陣而還者，無問多少，悉斬之。

translations.literal: When he faced the enemy he first sent one or two hundred men to attack; if they broke the line, so be it; if they could not break it and returned, no matter how many, all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the enemy he first sent one or two hundred men to charge; if they broke through, well and good—if they returned without breaking through, all were beheaded, however many.

sentences.zh: 又令三二百人複進，還如向法。

translations.literal: He then sent another two or three hundred men forward; if they returned, the same rule applied.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sent two or three hundred more; the same rule applied if they returned.

sentences.zh: 將士股慄，有必死之心，由是戰無不勝，稱為名將。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers' thighs trembled; they had the mind of certain death; hence in battle there was no defeat, and he was called a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers trembled with fear, resolved to die; hence he never lost a battle and was hailed as a famous general.

sentences.zh: 素時貴幸，言無不從，其從素征伐者，微功必錄，至於他將，雖有大功，多為文吏所譴卻。

translations.literal: At that time Su was favored and trusted; his words were never refused. Those who followed Su on campaign had even slight merit recorded; as for other generals, though they had great merit, they were mostly rejected by the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Su was then so favored that his word always stood; followers on campaign had even small deeds recorded, while other generals' great feats were often struck down by clerks.

sentences.zh: 故素雖嚴忍，士亦以此願從焉。

translations.literal: Thus though Su was harsh and cruel, soldiers for this reason were willing to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Though harsh, Su won soldiers' willingness to follow because of this.

sentences.zh: 二十年，晉王廣為靈朔道行軍元帥，素為長史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when Prince of Jin Guang was campaign commander-in-chief of the Ling and Shu routes, Su was chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, when Prince of Jin Guang was Ling-Shu campaign commander, Su served as chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 王卑躬以交素。

translations.literal: The prince humbled himself to befriend Su.
translations.idiomatic: The prince humbled himself to win Su's friendship.

sentences.zh: 及為太子，素之謀也。

translations.literal: When he became heir apparent, it was through Su's plotting.
translations.idiomatic: When he became heir apparent, it was Su's doing.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，代高熲為尚書左僕射，賜良馬百匹，牝馬二百匹，奴婢百口。

translations.literal: At the start of Renshou he replaced Gao Jiong as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and was given a hundred fine horses, two hundred mares, and a hundred male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Renshou he replaced Gao Jiong as left vice director and received a hundred fine horses, two hundred mares, and a hundred servants.

sentences.zh: 其年，以素為行軍元帥，出雲州擊突厥，連破之。

translations.literal: That year Su was made campaign commander-in-chief, went out from Yun Province to strike the Turks, and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made campaign commander, marched from Yun Province against the Turks, and repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 突厥退走，率騎追躡，至夜而及之。

translations.literal: The Turks withdrew; he led cavalry in pursuit and caught up with them by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks withdrew; he pursued with cavalry and caught them by night.

sentences.zh: 將複戰，恐賊越逸，令其騎稍後。

translations.literal: About to fight again, fearing the bandits would escape, he ordered his cavalry to hang back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: About to fight again, fearing escape, he held his cavalry slightly back.

sentences.zh: 於是親將兩騎，並降突厥二人，與虜並行，不之覺也。

translations.literal: He then personally took two horsemen and two surrendered Turks and rode alongside the enemy without their noticing.
translations.idiomatic: He personally took two horsemen and two surrendered Turks and rode alongside the enemy unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 候其頓舍未定，趣後騎掩擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Waiting until their camp was not yet settled, he urged the rear cavalry to strike by surprise and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: When their camp was not yet settled, he signaled the rear cavalry to strike and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 自是突厥遠遁，磧南無復虜庭。

translations.literal: From then on the Turks fled far away, and south of the desert there was no longer a barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Turks fled far away, and south of the desert no Turk court remained.

sentences.zh: 以功進子玄感位爲柱國，玄縱爲淮南郡公。

translations.literal: For his merit Su's son Xuangan was further made Pillar of the State and Xuanzong Duke of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit Xuangan was made pillar of the state and Xuanzong duke of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 賞物二萬段。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with twenty thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with twenty thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 及獻皇后崩，山陵制度，多出於素。

translations.literal: When Empress Xian died, the regulations for the mountain tomb mostly came from Su.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xian died, the tomb regulations owed much to Su.

sentences.zh: 上善之，下詔曰：

translations.literal: The emperor approved and issued an edict:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and issued an edict:

sentences.zh: 君為元首，臣則股肱，共治萬姓，義同一體。

translations.literal: The ruler is the head; ministers are the arms and thighs; together they govern the myriad people—righteousness is one body.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the head and ministers the arms and thighs; together they govern the people as one body.

sentences.zh: 上柱國、尚書左僕射、仁壽宮大監、越國公素，志度恢弘，機鑒明遠，懷佐時之略，包經國之才。

translations.literal: Supreme Pillar of the State, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Supervisor of Renshou Palace, and Duke of Yue Su has broad resolve and clear, far-reaching judgment, harbors the strategy of aiding the age, and embraces the talent to govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme pillar, left vice director, Renshou Palace supervisor, and Duke of Yue Su has broad vision, far-reaching judgment, the strategy to aid the age, and talent to govern the state.

sentences.zh: 王業初基，霸圖肇建，策名委質，受脤出師，擒剪凶魁，克平虢、鄭。

translations.literal: When the royal enterprise was first founded and the hegemonic design newly begun, he pledged his name and loyalty, received the sacrificial flesh, went out as commander, captured and cut down the chief villains, and pacified Guo and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was first founded he pledged loyalty, took command, captured chief villains, and pacified Guo and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 頻承廟算，揚旍江表，每稟戎律，長驅塞陰，南指而吳越肅清，北臨而獯獫摧服。

translations.literal: Repeatedly entrusted with the temple's plans, he raised banners south of the Yangzi; each time he received military law, he drove far into the northern frontier; pointing south, Wu and Yue were cleared; pressing north, the Xiongnu were broken and subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly entrusted with imperial strategy, he raised banners on the Yangzi and drove deep into the northern frontier; southward Wu and Yue were cleared, northward the barbarians were broken.

sentences.zh: 自居端揆，參贊機衡，當朝正色，直言無隱。

translations.literal: Since occupying the chief minister's seat and assisting in the pivot of power, he has kept upright color at court and spoken straight without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister at the pivot of power he kept upright bearing at court and spoke without concealment.

sentences.zh: 論文則詞藻縱橫，語武則權奇間出。

translations.literal: In literary discussion his wording is rich and sweeping; in martial talk his stratagems are singular and unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In letters his prose runs rich and bold; in war his stratagems are singular and unexpected.

sentences.zh: 既文且武，唯朕所命，任使之處，夙夜無怠。

translations.literal: Both literary and martial—only as We command; in every post of appointment, no slackness day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Both literary and martial—only as We command; in every post, no slackness day or night.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后奄離六宮，遠日雲及，塋兆安厝，委素經營。

translations.literal: Empress Xian has departed the six palaces; the distant day draws near; the tomb site is settled and entrusted to Su to arrange.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xian has left the six palaces; the burial day draws near; the tomb site is entrusted to Su.

sentences.zh: 然葬事依禮，唯卜泉石，至如吉凶，不由於此。

translations.literal: Yet burial affairs follow ritual; only spring stones are divined—for good or ill, it does not depend on this.
translations.idiomatic: Burial follows ritual; only the spring stones are divined—fortune does not depend on this alone.

sentences.zh: 素義存奉上，情深體國，欲使幽明俱泰，寶祚無窮。

translations.literal: Su's righteousness rests in serving above; his feeling for the state runs deep; he wishes to make dark and bright alike at peace and the precious throne without end.
translations.idiomatic: Su's righteousness serves the throne; his devotion to the state runs deep; he wishes dark and bright alike at peace and the throne without end.

sentences.zh: 以為陰陽之書，聖人所作，禍福之理，特須審慎。

translations.literal: He holds that books of yin and yang were made by sages and that the principles of fortune and calamity must be especially carefully weighed.
translations.idiomatic: He holds yin-yang books to be sages' work and fortune and calamity to need careful weighing.

sentences.zh: 乃遍歷川原，親自占擇，纖介不善，即更尋求，志圖元吉，孜孜不已。

translations.literal: He traversed every river plain and personally divined and chose; if the least thing was not good he sought again; his aim was supreme good fortune, tirelessly without rest.
translations.idiomatic: He searched every river plain and divined in person; the slightest ill omen sent him searching again, tirelessly for supreme good fortune.

sentences.zh: 心力備盡，人靈協贊，遂得神皋福壤，營建山陵。

translations.literal: Mind and strength were fully exhausted; human and spirit assisted; thus he obtained a divine mound of blessed soil and built the mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Mind and strength exhausted, heaven and men assisting, he found a blessed mound and built the tomb.

sentences.zh: 論素此心，事極誠孝，豈與夫平戎定寇比其功業？

translations.literal: Considering this heart of Su's, the matter reaches utmost filial piety—how can it be compared with pacifying barbarians and settling bandits for merit?
translations.idiomatic: In this devotion his filial piety is supreme—how can it be weighed against pacifying barbarians and bandits?

sentences.zh: 非唯廊廟之器，實是社稷之臣，若不加褒賞，何以申茲勸勵？

translations.literal: Not only is he an instrument of the hall and temple—he is truly a minister of the altars of soil and grain; if he is not given special reward and praise, how can this encouragement be declared?
translations.idiomatic: He is not only hall-and-temple timber but a true pillar of the altars; without special reward, how declare such encouragement?

sentences.zh: 可別封一子義康郡公，邑萬戶，子子孫孫，承襲不絕。

translations.literal: One son may be separately enfeoffed as Duke of Yikang commandery with a fief of ten thousand households, generation after generation without end.
translations.idiomatic: One son may be separately enfeoffed Duke of Yikang with ten thousand households, to pass down forever.

sentences.zh: 餘如故。

translations.literal: The rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: The rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 並賜田三十頃，絹萬段，米萬石，金缽一，實以金，銀缽一，實以珠，並綾錦五百段。

translations.literal: He was also given thirty qing of fields, ten thousand bolts of silk, ten thousand shi of rice, one gold bowl filled with gold, one silver bowl filled with pearls, and five hundred bolts of gauze and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He also received thirty qing of land, ten thousand bolts of silk, ten thousand shi of rice, a gold bowl of gold, a silver bowl of pearls, and five hundred bolts of gauze and brocade.

sentences.zh: 時素貴寵日隆，其弟約、從父文思、弟文紀，及族父異，並尚書列卿。

translations.literal: At that time Su's favor and honor grew daily; his younger brother Yue, his father's younger cousin Wensi, his younger brother Wenji, and his clan elder Yi were all ministers and chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Su's favor grew daily; his brother Yue, cousin Wensi, brother Wenji, and clan elder Yi all held ministerial posts.

sentences.zh: 諸子無汗馬之勞，位至柱國、刺史。

translations.literal: His sons had no sweat-of-the-horse merit yet reached the ranks of Pillar of the State and governor.
translations.idiomatic: His sons, without battlefield merit, reached pillar of the state and governor.

sentences.zh: 家僮數千，後庭妓妾曳綺羅者以千數。

translations.literal: Household retainers numbered in the thousands; concubines and entertainers trailing in gauze and silk numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Household retainers numbered thousands; concubines in gauze and silk numbered thousands.

sentences.zh: 第宅華侈，制擬宮禁。

translations.literal: Mansions and residences were splendid and extravagant, modeled on the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Mansions were splendid, modeled on the palace.

sentences.zh: 有鮑亨者，善屬文，殷胄者，工草隸，並江南士人，因高智慧沒為家奴。

translations.literal: There were Bao Heng, skilled at composition, and Yin Zhou, adept at cursive and clerical script—both Jiangnan scholars who, through Gao Zhihui's defeat, became household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Heng, skilled at prose, and Yin Zhou, adept at cursive and clerical script—Jiangnan scholars enslaved after Gao Zhihui's defeat—served his household.

sentences.zh: 親戚故吏，布列清顯，素之貴盛，近古未聞。

translations.literal: Kinsmen and old subordinates filled clear and eminent posts; Su's glory and power were unmatched in recent ages.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and old subordinates filled eminent posts; Su's glory was unmatched in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 煬帝初為太子，忌蜀王秀，與素謀之，構成其罪，後竟廢黜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang had first become heir apparent he resented Prince of Shu Xiu; with Su he plotted, fabricated charges, and in the end had him deposed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang first became heir he resented Prince of Shu Xiu; with Su he fabricated charges and had him deposed.

sentences.zh: 朝臣有違忤者，雖至誠體國，如賀若弼、史萬歲、李綱、柳彧等，素皆陰中之。

translations.literal: Court ministers who opposed him—even those as sincerely devoted to the state as He Ruobi, Shi Wansui, Li Gang, and Liu Yu—Su all secretly struck at them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who opposed him—even sincere servants of state like He Ruobi, Shi Wansui, Li Gang, and Liu Yu—Su secretly undermined.

sentences.zh: 若有附會及親戚，雖無才用，必加進擢。

translations.literal: If there were flatterers or kinsmen, though without talent they were surely promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers and kinsmen, however untalented, were promoted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷靡然，莫不畏附。

translations.literal: The court bent like grass; none did not fear and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The court bent like grass; all feared and clung to him.

sentences.zh: 唯兵部尚書柳述，以帝婿之重，數於上前面折素。

translations.literal: Only Minister of War Liu Shu, by weight of being the emperor's son-in-law, repeatedly rebuked Su before the emperor's face.
translations.idiomatic: Only Minister of War Liu Shu, as the emperor's son-in-law, repeatedly rebuked Su to his face before the throne.

sentences.zh: 大理卿梁毗，抗表上言素作威作福。

translations.literal: Director of the Court of Judicial Review Liang Pi submitted a memorial saying Su was making authority and making blessings for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Judicial Review director Liang Pi memorialized that Su was arrogating authority and favor.

sentences.zh: 上漸疏忌之，後因出敕曰：「僕射國之宰輔，不可躬親細務，但三五日一度向省，評論大事。」

translations.literal: The emperor gradually grew distant and suspicious; later he issued an edict: "The Vice Director is the state's chief minister and cannot personally attend to petty affairs; he need only come to the ministry once every three or five days to discuss great matters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew distant and suspicious; later he issued an edict: "The vice director is chief minister and cannot handle petty affairs—come to the ministry once every few days to discuss great matters.

sentences.zh: 外示優崇，實奪之權也。

translations.literal: Outwardly showing special honor, in reality his power was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly honored, in reality stripped of power.

sentences.zh: 終仁壽之末，不復通判省事。

translations.literal: To the end of Renshou he no longer jointly handled routine business.
translations.idiomatic: Through the end of Renshou he no longer handled routine business.

sentences.zh: 上賜王公以下射，素箭為第一，上手以外國所獻金精盤，價直巨萬，以賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted archery to princes and dukes and down; Su's arrow was first; the emperor personally gave him a golden spirit dish of foreign tribute worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At an archery contest for princes and below Su's arrow ranked first; the emperor gave him a foreign golden spirit dish worth tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 四年，從幸仁壽宮，宴賜重疊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the emperor to Renshou Palace and received layered feasts and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he accompanied the emperor to Renshou Palace and received lavish feasts and gifts.

sentences.zh: 及上不豫，素與兵部尚書柳述、黃門侍郎元岩等入閤侍疾。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, Su with Minister of War Liu Shu, Palace Attendant Yuan Yan, and others entered the inner chamber to attend the illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Su entered the inner chamber with Minister of War Liu Shu and Palace Attendant Yuan Yan to attend him.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子入居大寶殿，慮上有不諱，須豫防擬，乃手自為書，封出問素。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent had moved into the Great Treasure Hall; fearing the emperor might die, he needed to prepare in advance and personally wrote a letter, sealed it, and sent it out to ask Su.
translations.idiomatic: The heir had moved into the Great Treasure Hall; fearing the worst, he wrote and sealed a letter himself and sent it to Su.

sentences.zh: 素錄出事狀以報太子。

translations.literal: Su copied out the situation and reported to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Su copied the situation and reported to the heir.

sentences.zh: 宮人誤送上所，上覽而大恚。

translations.literal: A palace woman mistakenly sent it to the emperor; the emperor read it and was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman mistakenly sent it to the emperor; he read it and was furious.

sentences.zh: 所寵陳貴人又言太子無禮。

translations.literal: The favored Lady Chen of the Inner Palace also said the heir apparent was disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Favored Lady Chen also said the heir was disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 上遂發怒，欲召庶人勇。

translations.literal: The emperor then grew angry and wished to summon the deposed heir Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and wished to summon deposed heir Yong.

sentences.zh: 太子謀之于素，素矯詔追東宮兵士帖上臺宿衛，門禁出入，並取宇文述、郭衍節度，又令張衡侍疾。

translations.literal: The heir apparent plotted with Su; Su forged an edict to recall Eastern Palace soldiers and post them to guard the upper platform, controlled gate access in and out, and put Yuwen Shu and Guo Yan in command; he also ordered Zhang Heng to attend the illness.
translations.idiomatic: The heir plotted with Su; Su forged an edict recalling Eastern Palace troops to guard the upper platform, controlled all gates, put Yuwen Shu and Guo Yan in command, and ordered Zhang Heng to attend the illness.

sentences.zh: 上以此日崩，由是頗有異論。

translations.literal: The emperor died that same day; for this there were afterward many differing opinions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died that same day; afterward many questioned what had happened.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒反，遣茹茹天保來據蒲州，燒斷河橋。

translations.literal: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, he sent Ruru Tianbao to seize Pu Province and burn and cut the river bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, he sent Ruru Tianbao to seize Pu Province and burn the river bridge.

sentences.zh: 又遣王聃子率數萬人並力拒守。

translations.literal: He also sent Wang Danzi to lead tens of thousands of men to resist together.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Wang Danzi with tens of thousands to resist together.

sentences.zh: 素將輕騎五千襲之，潛於渭口宵濟，遲明擊之，天保敗走，聃子懾而以城降。

translations.literal: Su led five thousand light cavalry to strike them, secretly crossed the Wei ford by night, and at daybreak attacked; Tianbao was defeated and fled, and Danzi, afraid, surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Su led five thousand light cavalry, crossed the Wei ford secretly by night, and at dawn attacked; Tianbao fled and Danzi surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 有詔征還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his recall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him.

sentences.zh: 初，素將行也，計日破賊，皆如所量。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Su was about to go, he calculated the days to defeat the bandits, and all matched his estimate.
translations.idiomatic: Before marching, Su calculated days to victory—and all matched.

sentences.zh: 帝於是以素為并州道行軍總管、河北安撫大使，率眾數萬討諒。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore made Su campaign commander-in-chief of the Bingzhou route and Commissioner for Pacification of Hebei, leading tens of thousands to attack Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Su Bingzhou-route campaign commander and Hebei pacification commissioner with tens of thousands to attack Liang.

sentences.zh: 時晉、絳、呂三州並為諒城守，素各以二千人縻之而去。

translations.literal: At that time Jin, Jiang, and Lü provinces all held out for Liang; Su left two thousand men each to pin them and went on.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Jiang, and Lü all held for Liang; Su left two thousand men each to pin them and marched on.

sentences.zh: 諒遣趙子開擁眾十余萬，策絕徑路，屯據高壁，佈陣五十裡。

translations.literal: Liang sent Zhao Zikai with more than a hundred thousand men to block the narrow path, hold the high ramparts, and spread formations for fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Zhao Zikai with over a hundred thousand to block the pass, hold high walls, and spread formations fifty li wide.

sentences.zh: 素令諸將以兵臨之，自引奇兵潛入霍山，緣崖谷而進，直指其營，一戰破之，殺傷數萬。

translations.literal: Su ordered the generals to press them with troops; he himself led picked men secretly into Huo Mountain, advanced along cliffs and ravines, struck straight at their camp, broke them in one battle, and killed and wounded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Su pressed with main forces while he secretly led picked men through Huo Mountain along cliffs to strike the camp; one battle killed and wounded tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 諒所署介州刺史梁修羅屯介休，聞素至，懼，棄城而走。

translations.literal: Liang's appointed Governor of Jie Province Liang Xiuluo held at Jiexiu; hearing Su had arrived, he was afraid and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Jie governor Liang Xiuluo held Jiexiu; hearing Su had come, he fled.

sentences.zh: 進至清源，去并州三十裡，諒率其將王世宗、趙子開、蕭摩訶等，眾且十萬，來拒戰。

translations.literal: Advancing to Qingyuan, thirty li from Bing Province, Liang led his generals Wang Shizong, Zhao Zikai, Xiao Mohe, and others with nearly a hundred thousand men to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingyuan, thirty li from Bing Province, Liang led Wang Shizong, Zhao Zikai, Xiao Mohe, and nearly a hundred thousand men to resist.

sentences.zh: 又擊破之，擒蕭摩訶。

translations.literal: Su again attacked and defeated them and captured Xiao Mohe.
translations.idiomatic: Su again defeated them and captured Xiao Mohe.

sentences.zh: 諒退保并州，素進兵圍之，諒窮蹙而降，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Liang withdrew to hold Bing Province; Su advanced and besieged it; Liang, hard pressed, surrendered, and the remaining factions were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Liang withdrew to Bing Province; Su besieged it; hard pressed, Liang surrendered and the rest were pacified.

sentences.zh: 帝遣素弟修武公約齎手詔勞素曰：

translations.literal: The emperor sent Su's younger brother Duke of Xiuwu Yue to bring a handwritten edict to comfort Su:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Su's brother Duke of Xiuwu Yue with a handwritten edict to comfort him:

sentences.zh: 我有隋之禦天下也，於今二十有四年，雖複外夷侵叛，而內難不作，修文偃武，四海晏然。

translations.literal: When We held the Sui realm under heaven, it has now been twenty-four years; though outer barbarians invaded and rebelled, internal trouble did not arise; culture was cultivated and arms laid aside, and the four seas were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: In holding the Sui realm these twenty-four years, though outer tribes rebelled, no internal trouble arose; we cultivated culture and rested arms, and the four seas were calm.

sentences.zh: 朕以不天，銜恤在疚，號天叩地，無所逮及。

translations.literal: We, lacking Heaven's favor, bear mourning in grief; we cry to Heaven and knock our heads on earth—nothing reaches or avails.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking Heaven's favor, We bear mourning in grief, crying to Heaven and knocking our brow on earth—nothing avails.

sentences.zh: 朕本以籓王，謬膺儲兩，複以庸虛，纂承鴻業。

translations.literal: We were originally a frontier prince, wrongly granted the heir's place, and again by our mediocrity succeeded the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: We were originally a frontier prince, wrongly made heir, and by mediocrity succeeded the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 天下者，先皇之天下也，所以戰戰兢兢，弗敢失墜，況複神器之重，生民之大哉！

translations.literal: The realm under heaven is the late emperor's realm under heaven; therefore We are fearful and trembling, not daring to lose it—how much more the weight of the sacred vessel and the greatness of the living people!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is the late emperor's realm; We tremble lest it fall—how much more the throne's weight and the people's greatness!

sentences.zh: 賊諒包藏禍心，自幼而長，羊質獸心，假託名譽，不奉國諱，先圖叛逆，違君父之命，成莫大之罪。

translations.literal: The rebel Liang harbored evil in his heart from youth; sheep's substance, beast's heart; he borrowed reputation falsely, did not observe the state's taboo, first plotted rebellion, disobeyed the lord and father's command, and accomplished a crime without measure.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Liang harbored evil from youth—sheep's hide, beast's heart—borrowed false fame, ignored the state's taboo, plotted rebellion, defied father and lord, and committed measureless crime.

sentences.zh: 誑惑良善，委任奸回，稱兵內侮，毒流百姓。

translations.literal: He deceived the good, entrusted the wicked, raised troops to insult within, and poison flowed among the people.
translations.idiomatic: He deceived the good, trusted the wicked, raised arms within, and poison spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 私假署置，擅相謀戮，小加大，少淩長，民怨神怒，眾叛親離，為惡不同，同歸於亂。

translations.literal: He privately borrowed titles and appointments, arbitrarily plotted killings; the small overbore the great, the young insulted the elder; the people resented and spirits were angry; masses rebelled and kin deserted—all evil unlike, alike ending in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He usurped titles, plotted killings at will, let small overbear great and young insult elder; people resented, spirits raged, masses rebelled and kin deserted—all evil alike ending in chaos.

sentences.zh: 朕寡兄弟，猶未忍及言，是故開關門而待寇，揖干戈而不發。

translations.literal: We have few brothers and still cannot bear to speak of it; therefore We opened the gate and waited for the invader and sheathed the weapons without striking.
translations.idiomatic: We have few brothers and could hardly speak of it; We opened the gates to the invader and sheathed arms without striking.

sentences.zh: 朕聞之，天生蒸民，為之置君，仰惟先旨，每以子民為念，朕豈得枕伏苫廬，顛而不救也！

translations.literal: We have heard that Heaven born the multitude and set rulers for them; looking up to the former intent, We always take the people as Our thought—how can We lie pillowed on the mourning mat, overturned, and not save them!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven born the people and set rulers over them; We always take the people to heart—how lie on the mourning mat overturned and not save them!

sentences.zh: 大義滅親，《春秋》高義，周旦以誅二叔，漢啟乃戮七籓，義在茲乎？

translations.literal: Great righteousness destroys kin—the Spring and Autumn Annals exalt this righteousness; the Duke of Zhou for this executed his two uncles; Han Wendi for this executed the seven princes—is not righteousness here?
translations.idiomatic: Great righteousness destroys kin—the Annals exalt it; the Duke of Zhou executed two uncles, Han Wendi the seven princes—is not righteousness here?

sentences.zh: 事不獲已，是以授公戎律，問罪太原。

translations.literal: The matter could not be avoided; therefore We entrusted to you military law and questioned guilt at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: It could not be avoided; We entrusted you with military law to question guilt at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 且逆子賊臣，何代不有，豈意今者，近出家國。

translations.literal: Rebellious sons and traitorous ministers—what age lacks them? Who thought that today it would come so close from Our own house and state?
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious sons and traitor ministers—what age lacks them? Who thought today it would come from Our own house?

sentences.zh: 所歎荼毒甫爾，便及此事。

translations.literal: What We lament is that poison had barely begun when it reached this.
translations.idiomatic: We lament that poison had barely begun when it reached this.

sentences.zh: 由朕不能和兄弟，不能安蒼生，德澤未弘，兵戈先動，賊亂者止一從，塗炭者乃眾庶。

translations.literal: Because We could not harmonize brothers and could not settle the common people, virtue and grace were not broad, yet arms moved first; the rebel was only one follower, yet the charred were the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Because We could not harmonize brothers or settle the people, grace was not broad yet arms moved first; one follower rebelled, yet the multitude were charred.

sentences.zh: 非唯寅畏天威，亦乃孤負付囑，薄德厚恥，愧乎天下。

translations.literal: Not only in reverent fear of Heaven's majesty—We also alone bear the entrusted charge; thin virtue, thick shame—We are ashamed before the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Not only in reverent fear of Heaven's majesty—We also bear the charge alone; thin virtue, thick shame before the realm.

sentences.zh: 公乃先朝功臣，勳庸克茂。

translations.literal: You are a former-court meritorious minister; achievements and glory are abundant.
translations.idiomatic: You are a meritorious minister of the former court; achievement and glory abound.

sentences.zh: 至如皇基草創，百物惟始，便匹馬歸朝，誠識兼至。

translations.literal: As when the royal foundation was first laid and all things were beginning, with one horse you returned to court—sincerity and discernment together reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was first founded, with one horse you returned to court—sincerity and discernment together supreme.

sentences.zh: 汴部鄭州，風卷秋籜，荊南塞北，若火燎原，早建殊勳，夙著誠節。

translations.literal: At Bian and Zheng the wind rolled autumn bamboo; south of Jing and north of the frontier it was like fire spreading over the plain; early you built extraordinary merit and long showed sincere loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian and Zheng the wind rolled autumn bamboo; on Jing's south and the frontier north fire spread over the plain—you early built extraordinary merit and long showed loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及獻替朝端，具瞻惟允，爰弼朕躬，以濟時難，昔周勃、霍光，何以加也！

translations.literal: When you assisted at court's end all looked to you with trust; you aided Our person to cross the age's difficulty—how could Zhou Bo and Huo Guang add to this!
translations.idiomatic: Assisting at court's end all trusted you; you aided Us through the age's difficulty—what could Zhou Bo or Huo Guang add?

sentences.zh: 賊乃竊據蒲州，關梁斷絕，公以少擊眾，指期平殄。

translations.literal: The bandit secretly held Pu Province; passes and bridges were cut; you with the few struck the many and fixed the day for complete destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel held Pu Province and cut passes; you with few struck many and fixed the day for annihilation.

sentences.zh: 高壁據嶺，抗拒官軍，公以深謀，出其不意，霧廓雲除，冰消瓦解，長驅北邁，直趣巢窟。

translations.literal: High walls held the ridges and resisted the official army; you with deep planning struck where they did not expect; mist cleared and clouds parted, ice melted and tiles shattered; you drove far north straight to the nest and lair.
translations.idiomatic: High walls on the ridges resisted the army; your deep planning struck unexpectedly; mist cleared, ice melted; you drove north straight to the nest.

sentences.zh: 晉陽之南，蟻徒數萬，諒不量力，猶欲舉斧。

translations.literal: South of Jinyang, ant-like masses numbered in the tens of thousands; Liang, not measuring his strength, still wished to raise the axe.
translations.idiomatic: South of Jinyang ant-like masses numbered tens of thousands; Liang, misjudging strength, still wished to raise the axe.

sentences.zh: 公以棱威外討，發憤於內，忘身殉義，親當矢石。

translations.literal: You with stern might attacked outward and anger flared within; forgetting self you died for righteousness and personally met arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: With stern might outward and anger within, you forgot self for righteousness and met arrows and stones in person.

sentences.zh: 兵刃暫交，魚潰鳥散，僵屍蔽野，積甲若山。

translations.literal: Blades crossed briefly; fish scattered and birds broke; corpses covered the wild, piled armor like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Blades briefly crossed; fish scattered, birds broke; corpses covered the wild, armor piled like mountains.

sentences.zh: 諒遂守窮城，以拒鈇鉞。

translations.literal: Liang then held the exhausted city to resist axes and halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Liang then held the exhausted city against axes and halberds.

sentences.zh: 公董率驍勇，四面攻圍，使其欲戰不敢，求走無路，智力俱盡，面縛軍門。

translations.literal: You directed the fierce and brave and attacked on four sides, so that they wished to fight but dared not, sought escape but had no road; wit and strength were exhausted and he bound himself at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: You led the fierce on four sides until they wished to fight but dared not, sought escape but found none; wit and strength exhausted, he bound himself at the gate.

sentences.zh: 斬將搴旗，伐叛柔服，元惡既除，東夏清晏，嘉庸茂績，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Beheading generals and capturing banners, punishing rebels and soothing the submitted—the chief villain removed, the eastern Xia cleared and tranquil; great merit and splendid achievement lie here.
translations.idiomatic: Beheading generals, capturing banners, punishing rebels and soothing submission—the chief villain removed, the east cleared; great merit lies here.

sentences.zh: 昔武安平趙，淮陰定齊，豈若公遠而不勞，速而克捷者也！

translations.literal: Formerly Wu An pacified Zhao and Huaiyin settled Qi—how can that compare with your reaching far without toil, swift yet victorious!
translations.idiomatic: Wu An pacified Zhao, Huaiyin settled Qi—how compare with your reaching far without toil, swift and victorious!

sentences.zh: 朕殷憂諒闇，不得親禦六軍，未能問道於上庠，遂使劬勞於行陣。

translations.literal: We in deep grief at the darkened ruler could not personally lead the six armies and could not inquire of the Way in the upper academy; thus labor fell on the marching ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In deep grief at the darkened ruler We could not lead the six armies or inquire of the Way at the academy; labor fell on the marching ranks.

sentences.zh: 言念於此，無忘寢食。

translations.literal: Speaking of this in thought, We forget sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of this We forget sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 公乃建累世之元勳，執一心之確志。

translations.literal: You have built merit of accumulated generations and hold a steadfast heart of one resolve.
translations.idiomatic: You have built merit of generations and hold a steadfast heart.

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰：「疾風知勁草，世亂有誠臣。」

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: "Strong grass knows the fierce wind; in an age of disorder there are loyal ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Strong grass knows the fierce wind; in disorder there are loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 公得之矣。

translations.literal: You have obtained this.
translations.idiomatic: You have obtained this.

sentences.zh: 乃銘之常鼎，豈止書勳竹帛哉！

translations.literal: To inscribe it on the eternal tripod—how could it stop at recording merit on bamboo and silk!
translations.idiomatic: To inscribe it on the eternal tripod—how could it stop at bamboo and silk!

sentences.zh: 功績克諧，哽歎無已。

translations.literal: Merit harmoniously achieved—We choke with sighs without end.
translations.idiomatic: Merit harmoniously achieved—We choke with endless sighs.

sentences.zh: 稍冷，公如宜。

translations.literal: It grows slightly cold; you are as you should be.
translations.idiomatic: It grows slightly cold; take care of yourself.

sentences.zh: 軍旅務殷，殊當勞慮，故遣公弟，指宣往懷。

translations.literal: Military affairs are pressing and should greatly trouble your thought; therefore We send your younger brother to convey Our former feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs press and must greatly trouble you; We send your brother to convey Our feeling.

sentences.zh: 迷塞不次。

translations.literal: Written in confusion, not in order.
translations.idiomatic: Written in haste, not in order.

sentences.zh: 素上表陳謝曰：

translations.literal: Su submitted a memorial of thanks:
translations.idiomatic: Su submitted a memorial of thanks:

sentences.zh: 臣自惟虛薄，志不及遠，州郡之職，敢憚劬勞，卿相之榮，無階覬望。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects on his emptiness and thinness; his will does not reach far; in prefecture and commandery posts he dares bear toil and labor, but the glory of minister and chancellor—your servant has no step by which to look toward it.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects on his emptiness; his will does not reach far; in prefecture posts he bears toil, but ministerial glory he dares not aspire to.

sentences.zh: 然時逢昌運，王業惟始，雖涓流赴海，誠心屢竭，輕塵集岳，功力蓋微。

translations.literal: Yet the age met a prosperous fortune and the royal enterprise was only beginning; though a trickle goes to the sea, sincerity repeatedly exhausted itself; though light dust gathers on a peak, effort was mostly slight.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the age was prosperous and the enterprise beginning; though a trickle reaches the sea, sincerity repeatedly exhausted itself; though dust gathers on a peak, effort was slight.

sentences.zh: 徒以南陽裡閭，豐沛子弟，高位重爵，榮顯一時。

translations.literal: Only because in the lanes of Nanyang and among the youths of Feng and Pei, high rank and heavy titles were glorious for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Only because among Nanyang lanes and Feng-Pei youths, high rank and heavy titles shone for a time.

sentences.zh: 遂複入處朝端，出總戎律，受文武之任，預帷幄之謀。

translations.literal: Then again he entered to occupy court's end and went out to command military law, receiving civil and martial appointment and sharing in the planning of the inner tent.
translations.idiomatic: Then again he entered court's end and went out to command armies, bearing civil and martial charge and sharing inner planning.

sentences.zh: 豈臣才能，實由恩澤。

translations.literal: How could it be your servant's ability? In truth it was by grace and favor.
translations.idiomatic: How could it be my ability? In truth by grace and favor.

sentences.zh: 欲報之德，義極昊天。

translations.literal: Wishing to repay this virtue, righteousness reaches to the vast sky.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to repay this grace, righteousness reaches the vast sky.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下照重離之明，養繼天之德，牧臣於疏遠，照臣以光暉，南服降枉道之書，春宮奉肅成之旨。

translations.literal: Bowing, your servant reflects that Your Majesty illumines the brilliance of double li, nurtures virtue that continues Heaven, herds your servant in remoteness and illumines him with radiance; the southern submission sent a letter bending the Way, and the Eastern Palace offered the edict of reverent completion.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing, your servant reflects that Your Majesty illumines double li, nurtures heaven-continuing virtue, herds me in remoteness and illumines me with radiance; the south sent bending letters, the Eastern Palace the edict of reverent completion.

sentences.zh: 然草木無識，尚榮枯候時，況臣有心，實自效無路。

translations.literal: Yet grass and trees without knowledge still honor withering and flourishing according to the season; how much more your servant with a heart that truly has no path to show effect.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees without knowledge still honor the seasons; how much more I, with heart yet no path to serve.

sentences.zh: 盡夜回徨，寢食慚惕，常懼朝露奄至，虛負聖慈。

translations.literal: All night turning in circles, sleep and food with shame and fear; constantly fearing the morning dew will suddenly arrive and vainly bear the sage's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: All night turning, eating and sleeping in shame and fear, lest the morning dew come suddenly and I vainly bear your kindness.

sentences.zh: 賊諒包藏禍心，有自來矣，因幸國哀，便肆凶逆，興兵晉、代，搖盪山東。

translations.literal: The rebel Liang harbored evil in his heart from long ago; taking advantage of the state's mourning he then let loose fierce rebellion, raising troops in Jin and Dai and shaking the mountains east of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel Liang long harbored evil; taking advantage of national mourning he let loose fierce rebellion, raising troops in Jin and Dai and shaking the east.

sentences.zh: 陛下拔臣于凡流，授臣以戎律，蒙心膂之寄，稟平亂之規。

translations.literal: Your Majesty plucked your servant from the common stream and entrusted him with military law, placing on him the trust of heart and spine and granting the plan to pacify disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty plucked me from the common stream, entrusted military law, placed heart-and-spine trust on me, and granted the plan to pacify disorder.

sentences.zh: 蕭王赤心，人皆以死，漢皇大度，天下爭歸，妖寇廓清，豈臣之力！

translations.literal: Prince Xiao had a red heart and all men took death; Han's emperor had great breadth and the realm contended to submit; demonic bandits were cleared—how could it be your servant's strength!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao had a red heart and all men died for him; Han's emperor had great breadth and the realm submitted; the demons were cleared—not by my strength!

sentences.zh: 曲蒙使臣弟約齎詔書問勞，高旨峻筆，有若天臨，洪恩大澤，便同海運。

translations.literal: Wrongly receiving the order that your servant's younger brother Yue should bring the edict to ask after and comfort; the high intent and stern brush were as if Heaven looked down; vast grace and great favor were like the sea's transport.
translations.idiomatic: Wrongly receiving your order that my brother Yue bring comfort; the high intent and stern brush were as Heaven looking down; vast grace like the sea's transport.

sentences.zh: 悲欣慚懼，五情振越，雖百殞微軀，無以一報。

translations.literal: Grief, joy, shame, and fear—the five feelings were shaken beyond bounds; though a hundred deaths of this petty body could not repay one part.
translations.idiomatic: Grief, joy, shame, and fear shook the five feelings; though I died a hundred deaths I could not repay one part.

sentences.zh: 其月還京師，因從駕幸洛陽，以素領營東京大監。

translations.literal: That month he returned to the capital and followed the emperor in visiting Luoyang; Su was made Grand Supervisor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That month he returned to the capital and followed the emperor to Luoyang; Su was made grand supervisor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 以平諒之功，拜其子萬石、仁行、侄玄挺皆儀同三司，賚物五萬段，綺羅千匹，諒之妓妾二十人。

translations.literal: For pacifying Liang's merit he was made his sons Wanshi and Renxing and his nephew Xuanting all Threefold Peerage; he was given fifty thousand bolts of goods, a thousand bolts of gauze and silk, and twenty of Liang's concubines and entertainers.
