translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Liang his sons Wanshi and Renxing and nephew Xuanting were made threefold peerage; he received fifty thousand bolts of goods, a thousand of gauze and silk, and twenty of Liang's concubines.

sentences.zh: 大業元年，遷尚書令，賜東京甲第一區，物二千段。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and given one first-rank residence in the Eastern Capital and two thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daye he became director of the Masters of Writing, received a first-rank Eastern Capital residence and two thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 尋拜太子太師，餘官如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; the rest of his posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent; other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 前後賞錫，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts before and after could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards before and after were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜司徒，改封楚公，真食二千五百戶。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Minister of Education and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chu with direct sustenance of two thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made minister of education and re-enfeoffed Duke of Chu with two thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其年，卒官。

translations.literal: That year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰景武，贈光祿大夫、太尉公、弘農河東絳郡臨汾文城河內汲郡長平上黨西河十郡太守。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Jingwu; posthumously made Grand Master for the Brilliant, Grand Marshal, and Governor of ten commanderies of Hongnong, Hedong, Jiang, Fen, Wen, Cheng, Henei, Ji, Changping, Shangdang, Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Jingwu; posthumously grand master for the brilliant, grand marshal, and governor of ten commanderies.

sentences.zh: 給轀車，班劍四十人，前後部羽葆鼓吹，粟麥五千石，物五千段。

translations.literal: A covered carriage was granted, forty men with halberds in escort, feathered banners and drums before and behind, five thousand shi of millet and wheat, and five thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: A covered carriage was granted, forty halberd escorts, feathered banners and drums before and behind, five thousand shi of grain, and five thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonial supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The director of ceremonial supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 帝又下詔曰：「夫銘功彝器，紀德豐碑，所以垂名跡於不朽，樹風聲於沒世。

translations.literal: The emperor also issued an edict: "To inscribe merit on ritual vessels and record virtue on rich steles is to leave name and trace undying and set wind and sound for ages after death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also issued an edict: "Inscribing merit on ritual vessels and virtue on rich steles leaves name undying and sets fame for ages after death.

sentences.zh: 故楚景武公素，茂績元勳，劬勞王室，竭盡誠節，協贊朕躬。

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Jingwu of Chu Su had abundant achievement as founding merit, toiled for the royal house, exhausted sincere loyalty, and harmoniously assisted Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Jingwu of Chu Su had founding merit, toiled for the house, exhausted loyalty, and harmoniously assisted Us.

sentences.zh: 故以道邁三傑，功參十亂。

translations.literal: Therefore his Way surpassed the Three Heroes and his achievement joined the Ten Disordered.
translations.idiomatic: His Way surpassed the Three Heroes and his achievement joined the Ten Disordered.

sentences.zh: 未臻遐壽，遽揖清徽。

translations.literal: Before reaching long life he suddenly withdrew his clear radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Before long life he suddenly withdrew his clear radiance.

sentences.zh: 春秋遞代，方綿歲祀，式播雕篆，用圖勳德，可立碑宰隧，以彰盛美。」

translations.literal: Seasons pass in succession; years stretch on; We spread carved inscription to picture meritorious virtue—a stele may be raised at the tomb path to display this splendid beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons pass, years stretch on; We spread carved inscription to picture merit—a stele may be raised at the tomb path to display this splendor.

sentences.zh: 素嘗以五言詩七百字贈番州刺史薛道衡，詞氣宏拔，風韻秀上，亦為一時盛作。

translations.literal: Su once gave Xue Daoheng, Governor of Fan Province, a five-character poem of seven hundred characters; the wording was grand and elevated, style and tone elegant and superior—it too was a celebrated work of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Su once gave Fan governor Xue Daoheng a five-character poem of seven hundred characters—wording grand, tone elegant—a celebrated work of the age.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒，道衡歎曰：「人之將死，其言也善，豈若是乎！」

translations.literal: Before long he died; Daoheng sighed: "When a man is about to die his words are good—could it be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died; Daoheng sighed, "When a man is about to die his words are good—could it be like this!

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 素雖有建立之策及平楊諒功，然特為帝所猜忌，外示殊禮，內情甚薄。

translations.literal: Though Su had founding plans and merit in pacifying Yang Liang, yet the emperor especially distrusted him; outwardly showing special ritual, inwardly his feeling was very thin.
translations.idiomatic: Though Su had founding plans and merit pacifying Yang Liang, the emperor especially distrusted him—outward special ritual, inward thin feeling.

sentences.zh: 太史言隋分野有大喪，因改封于楚。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer said Sui's allotted region would see great mourning; he therefore changed the enfeoffment to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The grand astrologer said Sui's allotted region would see great mourning; he therefore changed the enfeoffment to Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚與隋同分，欲以此厭當之。

translations.literal: Chu shares the same allotted region with Sui; he wished by this to avert and meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Chu shares Sui's allotted region; he wished by this to avert the omen.

sentences.zh: 素寢疾之日，帝每令名醫診候，賜以上藥。

translations.literal: On the days Su lay ill the emperor often sent famous physicians to examine and attend him and gave superior drugs.
translations.idiomatic: While Su lay ill the emperor often sent famous physicians and gave superior drugs.

sentences.zh: 然密問醫人，恆恐不死。

translations.literal: Yet he secretly asked the physicians and always feared he would not die.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he secretly asked the physicians and always feared Su would not die.

sentences.zh: 素又自知名位已極，不肯服藥，亦不將慎，每語弟約曰：「我豈須更活耶？」

translations.literal: Su also knew his name and rank had reached the limit and would not take medicine nor be careful; he often told his younger brother Yue: "Do I still need to live longer?"
translations.idiomatic: Su knew his rank had reached its limit, refused medicine and care, and often told his brother Yue, "Do I still need to live?

sentences.zh: 素貪冒財貨，營求產業。

translations.literal: Su was greedy for wealth and goods and schemed for estates.
translations.idiomatic: Su was greedy for wealth and schemed for estates.

sentences.zh: 東、西二京，居宅侈麗，朝毀夕複，營繕無已。

translations.literal: In the eastern and western capitals his dwellings were lavish; torn down in the morning and rebuilt in the evening, construction without end.
translations.idiomatic: In both capitals his dwellings were lavish—torn down mornings, rebuilt evenings, construction without end.

sentences.zh: 爰及諸方都會處，邸店、水磑並利田宅以千百數，時議以此鄙之。

translations.literal: Reaching every major city and junction, inns, water mills, and profitable fields and houses numbered in the hundreds and thousands; opinion at the time despised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: At every major city, inns, mills, and profitable lands numbered in hundreds and thousands; opinion despised him for this.

sentences.zh: 子玄感嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Xuangan succeeded him; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuangan succeeded him; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆坐玄感誅死。

translations.literal: All his sons were executed because of Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: All his sons were executed because of Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 約字惠伯，素異母弟也。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Huibo, was Su's younger brother by a different mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, styled Huibo, was Su's younger brother by a different mother.

sentences.zh: 在童兒時，嘗登樹墮地，為查所傷，由是竟為宦者。

translations.literal: When still a child he once climbed a tree and fell; a splinter wounded him, and for this he ended as a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he climbed a tree, fell on a splinter, and became a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 性好沉靜，內多譎詐，好學強記。

translations.literal: By nature he loved quiet and was inwardly full of deceit; he loved learning and had a strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved quiet and was inwardly deceitful; he loved learning and remembered strongly.

sentences.zh: 素友愛之，凡有所為，必先籌於約而後行之。

translations.literal: Su treated him with brotherly affection; whatever Su did always had first to be planned with Yue and then carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Su loved him as a brother; whatever Su did was first planned with Yue.

sentences.zh: 在週末，以素軍功，賜爵安成縣公，拜上儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou, because of Su's military merit, he was given the title Duke of Ancheng county with a fief of five hundred households and appointed Upper Threefold Peerage.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhou's end, for Su's military merit, he was made Duke of Ancheng with five hundred households and upper threefold peerage.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，授長秋卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu accepted the abdication he was appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed director of the palace domestic service.

sentences.zh: 久之，為邵州刺史，入為宗正少卿，轉大理少卿。

translations.literal: After a long time he was Governor of Shao Province, entered as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was governor of Shao, vice director of the imperial clan, then vice director of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子無寵，而晉王廣規欲奪宗，以素幸於上，而雅信約。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent had no favor, while Prince of Jin Guang plotted to seize the succession; because Su was favored by the emperor and deeply trusted Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The heir had no favor while Prince of Jin Guang plotted the succession; Su was favored by the emperor and deeply trusted Yue.

sentences.zh: 於是用張衡計，遣宇文述大以金寶賂遺於約，因通王意，說之曰：「夫守正履道，固人臣之常致，反經合義，亦達者之令圖。

translations.literal: Thereupon using Zhang Heng's plan they sent Yuwen Shu with great gold and treasure to bribe Yue, and through him connected with the prince's intent, saying to him: "To keep upright and tread the Way is indeed the common attainment of ministers; to go against the canon and join with righteousness is also the excellent scheme of the far-seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Using Zhang Heng's plan they sent Yuwen Shu with great gold and treasure to bribe Yue and connect with the prince, saying: "Keeping upright is a minister's common duty; going against canon for righteousness is also the far-seeing man's excellent scheme.

sentences.zh: 自古賢人君子，莫不與時消息，以避禍患。

translations.literal: From ancient times worthy men and gentlemen have all moved with the times to avoid disaster and harm.
translations.idiomatic: From ancient times worthy men have moved with the times to avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 公之兄弟，功名蓋世，當途用事，有年歲矣。

translations.literal: Your brothers' achievement and fame cover the age; they hold power on the road and have for years.
translations.idiomatic: Your brothers' fame covers the age; they hold power for years.

sentences.zh: 朝臣為足下家所屈辱者，可勝數哉！

translations.literal: Court ministers whom your household has humiliated—can they be counted!
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers your house has humiliated—can they be counted!

sentences.zh: 又儲宮以所欲不行，每切齒於執政。

translations.literal: Also the heir apparent, because his wishes are not carried out, gnashes teeth at those in power.
translations.idiomatic: The heir, his wishes denied, gnashes teeth at those in power.

sentences.zh: 公雖自結於人主，而欲危公者固亦多矣。

translations.literal: Though you attach yourself to the lord, those who wish to harm you are indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: Though you attach to the lord, many wish you harm.

sentences.zh: 主上一旦棄群臣，公亦何以取庇？

translations.literal: If the lord one day abandons his ministers, how will you find shelter?
translations.idiomatic: If the lord one day abandons his ministers, how will you find shelter?

sentences.zh: 今皇太子失愛于皇后，主上素有廢黜之心，此公所知也。

translations.literal: Now the heir apparent has lost the empress's love; the lord has long had the mind to depose him—you know this.
translations.idiomatic: The heir has lost the empress's love; the lord long wished to depose him—you know this.

sentences.zh: 今若請立晉王，在賢兄之口耳。

translations.literal: Now if you ask to install Prince of Jin, it is only a word from your worthy elder brother's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: To install Prince of Jin needs only a word from your elder brother.

sentences.zh: 誠能因此時建大功，王必鐫銘於骨髓，斯則去累卵之危，成太山之安也。」

translations.literal: If you can truly at this time establish great merit, the prince will surely inscribe it in marrow and bone; then you remove the danger of piled eggs and achieve the security of Mount Tai."
translations.idiomatic: Establish great merit now and the prince will inscribe it in bone; you remove egg-pile danger and gain Mount Tai's security.

sentences.zh: 約然之，因以白素。

translations.literal: Yue agreed and therefore told Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yue agreed and told Su.

sentences.zh: 素本兇險，聞之大喜，乃撫掌而對曰：「吾之智思，殊不及此，賴汝起予。」

translations.literal: Su by nature was fierce and dangerous; hearing this he was greatly pleased and, clapping his hands, answered: "My wisdom and thought fall far short of this; I rely on you to awaken me."
translations.idiomatic: Su, fierce by nature, was delighted and clapped his hands: "My wit falls short; I rely on you to awaken me.

sentences.zh: 約知其計行，複謂素曰：「今皇后之言，上無不用，宜因機會，早自結托，則匪唯長保榮祿，傳祚子孫，又晉王傾身禮士，聲名日盛，躬履節儉，有主上之風，以約料之，必能安天下。

translations.literal: Yue knew his plan would succeed and again told Su: "Now the empress's words—the emperor uses none he rejects; you should by this opportunity early attach yourself, then not only long preserve rank and salary and pass it to descendants—Prince of Jin bows body and honors scholars, his fame grows daily, personally practicing frugality with the lord's bearing; by Yue's reckoning he can surely settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yue knew the plan would work and said again: "The empress's words the emperor never rejects; attach early and you preserve rank for descendants—Prince of Jin honors scholars, grows in fame, practices frugality like the lord; by my reckoning he can settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 兄若遲疑，一旦有變，令太子用事，恐禍至無日矣。」

translations.literal: If you, elder brother, hesitate, once there is change and the heir holds power, I fear disaster will come within days."
translations.idiomatic: Hesitate, and once the heir holds power disaster may come within days.

sentences.zh: 素遂行其策，太子果廢。

translations.literal: Su then carried out this plan and the heir apparent was indeed deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Su carried out the plan and the heir was deposed.

sentences.zh: 後帝在東都，令約詣京師享廟，行至華陰，見其兄墓，遂枉道拜哭，為憲司所劾，坐是免官。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor was at the Eastern Capital he ordered Yue to go to the capital to offer at the ancestral temple; reaching Huayin he saw his elder brother's tomb, turned aside from the road to bow and weep, and was impeached by the censorate and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor at the Eastern Capital ordered Yue to the capital for ancestral rites; at Huayin he saw his brother's tomb, turned aside to bow and weep, was impeached by the censorate, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜淅陽太守。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Governor of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 其兄子玄感，時為禮部尚書，與約恩義甚篤。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Xuangan was then Minister of Rites; with Yue his righteous bond was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Xuangan was then minister of rites; with Yue his bond was very deep.

sentences.zh: 既愴分離，形於顏色，帝謂之曰：「公比憂瘁，得非為叔邪？」

translations.literal: Already grieved at separation, it showed on his face; the emperor said to him: "You seem more troubled than usual—is it not because of your uncle?"
translations.idiomatic: Grief at parting showed on his face; the emperor said, "You seem troubled—is it your uncle?

sentences.zh: 玄感再拜流涕曰：「誠如聖旨。」

translations.literal: Xuangan twice bowed with tears and said: "It is truly as Your Majesty says."
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan bowed with tears: "It is truly as Your Majesty says."

sentences.zh: 帝亦思約廢立功，由是征入朝。

translations.literal: The emperor also remembered Yue's merit in deposing the heir and therefore summoned him to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered Yue's merit deposing the heir and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，以素子玄挺後之。

translations.literal: Before long he died; Su's son Xuanting was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died; Su's son Xuanting was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 從父文思

translations.literal: Father's younger cousin Wensi
translations.idiomatic: Su's father's younger cousin Wensi

sentences.zh: 文思字溫才，素從叔也。

translations.literal: Wensi, styled Wencai, was Su's father's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi, styled Wencai, was Su's father's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 父寬，魏左僕射，周小塚宰。

translations.literal: His father Kuan was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Wei and Minor Grand Minister under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuan was Wei left vice director and Zhou minor grand minister.

sentences.zh: 文思在周，年十一，拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Wensi under Zhou, at age eleven, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Threefold Peerage, and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou, at eleven Wensi was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, threefold peerage, and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋以父功，封新豐縣子，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon because of his father's merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinfeng with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon for his father's merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xinfeng with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天和初，治武都太守，十姓獠反，文思討平之，複治翼州事。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianhe he governed as Administrator of Wudu; the Ten-Surname Liao rebelled and Wensi pacified them, and again he governed Yi Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianhe's start he governed Wudu; the Ten-Surname Liao rebelled and he pacified them, then governed Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 党項羌叛，文思率州兵討平之。

translations.literal: The Tangut Qiang rebelled; Wensi led provincial troops and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut Qiang rebelled; Wensi led provincial troops and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 進擊資中、武康、隆山生獠及東山獠，並破之。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack the raw Liao of Zizhong, Wukang, Longshan, and the eastern mountain Liao and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against raw Liao of Zizhong, Wukang, Longshan, and the eastern mountains and broke them all.

sentences.zh: 後從陳王攻齊河陰城，又從武帝攻拔晉州，以勳進授上儀同三司，改封永寧縣公，增邑至千戶。

translations.literal: Later he followed Prince of Chen to attack Qi at Heyin city and followed Emperor Wu to capture Jin Province; for merit he was made Upper Threefold Peerage, re-enfeoffed Duke of Yongning with fief increased to a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince of Chen against Qi at Heyin and Emperor Wu to capture Jin; for merit he became upper threefold peerage and Duke of Yongning with a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 壽陽劉叔仁作亂，從清河公宇文神舉討之，戰于磚井，在陣生擒叔仁。

translations.literal: Liu Shuren of Shouyang rebelled; he followed Duke of Qinghe Yuwen Shenju to attack him; fighting at Zhuanjing he captured Shuren alive in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shuren of Shouyang rebelled; following Duke of Qinghe Yuwen Shenju he captured Shuren alive at Zhuanjing.

sentences.zh: 又別從王誼破賊於鯉魚柵。

translations.literal: He also separately followed Wang Yi and defeated bandits at Liyu palisade.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Wang Yi and defeated bandits at Liyu palisade.

sentences.zh: 其後累以軍功，遷果毅右旅下大夫。

translations.literal: Afterward he repeatedly by military merit was transferred to Right Brigade Deputy Commander of Determined Courage.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward by repeated military merit he became right brigade deputy commander of determined courage.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬拒尉迥于武陟。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor he followed Wei Xiaokuan to resist Wei Chiyuan at Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Wei Chiyuan at Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 迥遣其將李圍俊懷州，與行軍總管宇文述擊走之。

translations.literal: Chiyuan sent his general Li Weijun against Huai Province; with campaign commander Yuwen Shu he drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Chiyuan sent Li Weijun against Huai; with campaign commander Yuwen Shu he drove him off.

sentences.zh: 破尉惇，平鄴城，皆有功，進授上大將軍，改封洛川縣公。

translations.literal: He broke Wei Dun and pacified Ye city—all with merit; he was further made Grand General and re-enfeoffed Duke of Luochuan.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Wei Dun and pacified Ye—all with merit; he was further made grand general and Duke of Luochuan.

sentences.zh: 尋拜隆州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was governor of Long Province.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，進爵正平郡公，加邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was advanced to Duke of Zhengping with fief increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaihuang he was advanced Duke of Zhengping with two thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 後為魏州刺史，甚有惠政，及去職，吏民思之，為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Later he was Governor of Wei Province with very benevolent governance; when he left office officials and people missed him and raised a stele to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later as Wei governor he governed benevolently; when he left, officials and people raised a stele praising him.

sentences.zh: 轉冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，征為民部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned as Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was summoned minister of the household.

sentences.zh: 轉納言，改授右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and reappointed Right Grand Master for the Brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Masters of Writing and right grand master for the brilliant.

sentences.zh: 從幸江都宮，以足疾不堪趨奏，複授民部尚書，加位左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Jiangdu Palace, because of foot ailment he could not attend audience; he was again appointed Minister of the Household and further made Left Grand Master for the Brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangdu Palace foot ailment kept him from audience; he was again minister of the household and left grand master for the brilliant.

sentences.zh: 卒官，時年七十。

translations.literal: He died in office at age seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at seventy.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 初，文思當襲父爵，自以非嫡，遂讓封于弟文紀，當世多之。

translations.literal: Earlier Wensi should have inherited his father's title; considering himself not the legitimate son he yielded the enfeoffment to his younger brother Wenji; the age mostly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi should have inherited his father's title; considering himself not legitimate he yielded to brother Wenji; the age praised him.

sentences.zh: 文思弟文紀

translations.literal: Wensi's younger brother Wenji
translations.idiomatic: Wensi's younger brother Wenji

sentences.zh: 文紀字溫范，少剛正，有器局。

translations.literal: Wenji, styled Wenfan, from youth was upright and firm with capacity and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji, styled Wenfan, from youth was upright and firm with capacity.

sentences.zh: 在周襲爵華山郡公，邑二千七百戶。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Huashan commandery with a fief of two thousand seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he inherited Duke of Huashan with two thousand seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 自右侍上士累遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、安州總管長史。

translations.literal: From Right Attendant Upper Clerk he was repeatedly promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Threefold Peerage, and Chief of Staff to the Commander-in-Chief of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: From right attendant upper clerk he rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry, threefold peerage, and chief of staff to An Province's commander.

sentences.zh: 將兵迎陳降將李瑗于齊安，與陳將周法尚軍遇，擊走之。

translations.literal: He led troops to welcome Chen's surrendering general Li Yuan at Qi'an; he met Chen general Zhou Fashang's army and drove it off.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to welcome Chen surrendering general Li Yuan at Qi'an and drove off Chen general Zhou Fashang.

sentences.zh: 以功進授開府，入為虞部下大夫。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Colonel Opening the State and entered as Deputy Director under the Masters of Works.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made colonel opening the state and deputy under the masters of works.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，改封汾陰縣公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor he was re-enfeoffed Duke of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 從梁睿討王謙，以功進授上大將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Liang Rui to attack Wang Qian and for merit was further made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liang Rui against Wang Qian and for merit was further made grand general.

sentences.zh: 前後增邑三千戶。

translations.literal: Before and after his fief was increased by three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after his fief increased by three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 拜資州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Zi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Zi Province.

sentences.zh: 入為宗正少卿，坐事除名。

translations.literal: He entered as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as vice director of the imperial clan and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後數載，複其爵位，拜熊州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later his title and rank were restored and he was appointed Governor of Xiong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his title was restored and he was governor of Xiong Province.

sentences.zh: 改封上明郡公。

translations.literal: He was re-enfeoffed Duke of Shangming.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed Duke of Shangming.

sentences.zh: 除宗正卿。

translations.literal: He was removed as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 兼給事黃門侍郎，判禮部尚書事。

translations.literal: He also served as Attendant of Affairs and Yellow Gate and concurrently judged the affairs of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as attendant of affairs and yellow gate and judged Ministry of Rites affairs.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年，遷荊州總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renshou he was transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou year 2 he was transferred commander of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒官，時年五十八。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died in office at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he died in office at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：楊素少而輕俠，俶儻不羈，兼文武之資，包英奇之略，志懷遠大，以功名自許。

translations.literal: The historian says: Yang Su in youth was light and chivalrous, bold and unrestrained; he combined civil and martial endowment and embraced heroic stratagem, with ambition reaching far and taking achievement and fame as his pledge.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Yang Su in youth was light and chivalrous, bold and unrestrained; he combined civil and martial gifts and heroic stratagem, ambition reaching far, achievement and fame his pledge.

sentences.zh: 高祖龍飛，將清六合，許以腹心之奇，每當推彀之重。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose like a dragon to clear the six harmonies, he was promised the marvel of heart and belly; each time he bore the weight of the push-car.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose to clear the realm he was promised heart-and-belly trust; each time he bore the push-car's weight.

sentences.zh: 掃妖氛于牛鬥，江海無波；

translations.literal: He swept demonic vapors from the Ox Dipper; rivers and seas had no waves;
translations.idiomatic: He swept demonic vapors from the Ox Dipper; rivers and seas had no waves;

sentences.zh: 摧驍騎于龍庭，匈奴遠遁。

translations.literal: he crushed fierce cavalry at the Dragon Court; the Xiongnu fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: he crushed fierce cavalry at the Dragon Court; the Xiongnu fled far away.

sentences.zh: 考其夷凶靜亂，功臣莫居其右；

translations.literal: Examining his pacifying the fierce and settling disorder, no meritorious minister stands to his right;
translations.idiomatic: Examining his pacifying the fierce and settling disorder, no meritorious minister stands above him;

sentences.zh: 覽其奇策高文，足為一時之傑。

translations.literal: reading his singular plans and elevated prose, he was fully a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: reading his singular plans and elevated prose, he was fully a hero of the age.

sentences.zh: 然專以智詐自立，不由仁義之道，阿諛時主，高下其心。

translations.literal: Yet he relied solely on craft and fraud to establish himself, not by the Way of humaneness and righteousness; he flattered the lord of the age and raised or lowered his heart accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he relied on craft and fraud, not humaneness and righteousness; he flattered the lord and bent his heart accordingly.

sentences.zh: 營構離宮，陷君於奢侈；

translations.literal: He constructed detached palaces and trapped the lord in extravagance;
translations.idiomatic: He built detached palaces and trapped the lord in extravagance;

sentences.zh: 謀廢塚嫡，致國于傾危。

translations.literal: he plotted to depose the heir and brought the state to leaning peril.
translations.idiomatic: he plotted to depose the heir and brought the state to peril.

sentences.zh: 終使宗廟丘墟，市朝霜露，究其禍敗之源，實乃素之由也。

translations.literal: In the end the ancestral temple became a mound and market and court knew dew and frost; examining the source of disaster and ruin, in truth it was because of Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the ancestral temple became a mound and court knew dew and frost; examining disaster's source, in truth it was Su.

sentences.zh: 幸而得死，子為亂階，墳土未幹，闔門殂戮，丘隴發掘，宗族誅夷。

translations.literal: Fortunate to obtain death, his son became the stair of disorder; before the grave earth was dry the whole gate was slaughtered, the mound was dug up, and the clan executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunate to die himself, his son became disorder's stair; before grave earth dried the whole gate was slaughtered, the mound dug, the clan executed.

sentences.zh: 則知積惡餘殃，信非徒語。

translations.literal: Then one knows accumulated evil's remaining calamity is truly not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: Then one knows accumulated evil's remaining calamity is no empty talk.

sentences.zh: 多行無禮必自及，其斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: Much unprincipled conduct must rebound on oneself—is this not what is meant!
translations.idiomatic: Much unprincipled conduct must rebound on oneself—is this not what is meant!

sentences.zh: 約外示溫柔，內懷狡算，為蛇畫足，終傾國本，俾無遺育，宜哉！

translations.literal: Yue outwardly showed gentleness yet inwardly harbored cunning calculation; adding feet to the snake he finally overturned the state's foundation, leaving no descendants—fit indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Yue outwardly gentle yet inwardly cunning, adding feet to the snake he overturned the state's foundation and left no descendants—fit indeed!
